chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

"When you intend to leave the city, perform ghusl, then go to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) after you have finished your needs, bid him farewell, and do as you did when you entered.
And say: O God, do not make it the last visitation to the grave of Your Prophet. If You cause me to die before that, then indeed I bear witness in my death upon what I bore witness to in my life.
That there is no god but You, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger, peace be upon him and his family.

key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: The city (specifically Medina in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and ritual when leaving Medina after visiting the Prophet's grave?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the ritual etiquette (adab) for departing from Medina, emphasizing the spiritual significance of the Prophet's grave as a place of witness and covenant. The supplication reflects the Shia belief in the continuity of faith beyond death, linking the final testimony of faith (kalimah) to the specific context of visiting the Prophet, thereby reinforcing the concept of *Wada'* (farewell) as a solemn spiritual commitment.
